section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the maamar to the Maggid's teaching on the verse "Vayeishev Yaakov," explaining that Yaakov's descent to settle in the land is for the purpose of gathering holy sparks.
section.t: And this can be connected with the teaching of the Maggid
(whose yahrtzeit is observed)
on the verse,
"And Yaakov settled in the land of his father's sojournings, in the land of Canaan,"
[namely,] that Yaakov's descent from his supernal level to settle in the land, in materiality
(that is,
the descent of the soul below)
[even to the degree of "vayeishev,"
for "yeshivah" (sitting) is only an expression of delay],
is for the sake of "megurei aviv,"
"megurei" being an expression of gathering and ingathering, like "oger bakayitz" (one who gathers in summer),
to gather and collect the holy sparks
(that are in this world)
and to bring them in and elevate them upward.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the Maggid's two interpretations of "megurei aviv"—fear of Heaven and gathering sparks—corresponding to the two purposes of the soul's descent.
section.t: And behold, in the teaching of the aforementioned Maggid, at its beginning,
he explains
that "megurei aviv" is the fear of his Father in Heaven
("megurei" being an expression of terror and fear),
and the interpretation of "And Yaakov settled in the land of his father's sojournings, etc." is
that although he is in the land,
in the materiality and physicality of this world
[and moreover,
that in this world itself he is in the land of Canaan, from the expression "Canaan, in his hand are deceitful scales,"
meaning that he is found among the wicked],
nevertheless, he is in "megurei aviv,"
in the fear of his Father in Heaven.
And after this, he adds another interpretation,
that "megurei aviv" is the gathering of the sparks, as above.
And it can be said
that these two interpretations are the two matters
(of section 6 above)
that are accomplished through the descent of the soul below.
For first, he explains the elevation that occurs in the soul through its descent below,
that by the fact that even when it is in the materiality and physicality of this world
[and moreover—in the land of Canaan]
it is in fear of Heaven,
through this it is elevated more than it was before its descent.
[And particularly according to what is explained in Torah Ohr, the discourse "Vayeishev Yaakov"
(and in the glosses of the Tzemach Tzedek there),
that by the soul overcoming the concealments and veils of the body and the time of exile and arousing itself with love and fear,
the love and fear themselves are also more elevated than the love and fear before its descent.]
And afterwards, he explains a more exalted matter that is accomplished through the descent of the soul below,
for this matter is the ultimate purpose of the descent,
to gather and collect the holy sparks and elevate them upward.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the interpretation of "megurei aviv" as gathering sparks is connected to the interpretation of fear, because the perfection of refining sparks is achieved through the service of fear and self-nullification as a servant.
section.t: And it can be said

that the interpretation of "megurei aviv" as the gathering and ingathering of the sparks comes in continuation and connection with the interpretation that "megurei aviv" is the fear of his Father in Heaven.
[And the connection of the two interpretations is also understood from what is explained in Torah Ohr there,
that the two interpretations of "megurei,"
an expression of fear and an expression of a treasury,
both coincide.
And although in Torah Ohr there,
even according to the interpretation that "megurei" is an expression of a treasury,
"megurei" refers to fear
(as it is written,
"Fear of Hashem is His treasury,"
and likewise in the words of our sages,
"a treasury of fear of Heaven"),
it can be said
that the connection of the two interpretations is also according to the explanation in the teaching of the Maggid that "megurei," an expression of gathering and ingathering
(a treasury),
refers to the gathering of the sparks].
For the perfection of the refinement and elevation of the sparks
("megurei," an expression of gathering)
is through the service of fear,
the self-nullification of a servant,
whose entire intention in his service is
(not for himself,
nor even in order to cleave to Him, etc.,
but only)
to serve his Master,
to make a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He, in the lower realms,
and through this the refinement is in perfection.
